title: Leveraging Critical Proof Obligations for Efficient IC3 Verification
problem: IC3 model-checking methods spend significant effort tracking proof obligations (states to prove unreachable), creating a bottleneck in hardware verification performance due to inefficient proof obligation management.
method: Introduces Critical Proof Obligations (CPOs) that identify high-impact proof obligations, and applies two techniques: CPO-Driven UNSAT Core Generation to extract minimal sets of constraints, and CPO-Driven Proof Obligation Propagation to accelerate frame refinement and lemma discovery.

title: PHOENIX: Pauli-Based High-Level Optimization Engine for Instruction Execution on NISQ Devices
problem: Variational quantum algorithms require compilation at gate level, missing high-level Pauli-based optimization opportunities for Hamiltonian simulation programs.
method: PHOENIX operates on Pauli-based IR using binary symplectic form (BSF) to formally describe Pauli strings. It reformulates IR synthesis as BSF column-weight reduction via Clifford transformations, with heuristic simplification searching for optimal 2Q operators and TETRIS-like global ordering.

title: MOSS: Multi-Modal Representation Learning on Sequential Circuits
problem: Circuit representation learning faces tradeoffs: LLMs understand RTL functionality but struggle with low-level netlist behavior; GNNs model netlists but fail on large sequential circuits due to long-range dependencies.
method: MOSS fuses GNNs with LLMs: enhances D-type flip-flop (DFF) node features using fine-tuned LLM embeddings from RTL; GNN operates on reduced anchor points reducing long-range dependency burden; LLM provides global circuit embeddings for supervision; adaptive aggregation and two-phase propagation for signal modeling.

title: InstAttention: In-Storage Attention Offloading for Cost-Effective Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: Long-context LLM inference at large batch sizes generates KV caches that exceed GPU VRAM capacity; offloading KV caches to SSDs via PCIe creates a critical bandwidth bottleneck that severely limits throughput.
method: InstAttention offloads both the attention computation and KV cache storage to Computational Storage Drives (CSDs), which have high internal NAND bandwidth not limited by PCIe. A flash-aware in-storage attention engine executes the attention decode phase directly inside the CSD, with KV cache management mechanisms tailored to flash access patterns (e.g., large sequential reads). Optimized P2P transmission between GPU and CSDs eliminates unnecessary data migration back across PCIe. The system targets offline inference of a 13B model on an NVIDIA A6000 GPU.

title: To Tackle Cost-Skew Tradeoff: An Adaptive Learning Approach for Hub Node Selection
problem: Clock tree skew is a critical performance limiter in chip design; achieving good balance between total wire-length cost and skew requires selecting optimal hub nodes, but this combinatorial optimization is hard to solve optimally at large scale.
method: Proposes reinforcement learning-based method for hub node selection with adaptive learning strategy. The RL agent learns to select hub nodes that optimize the cost-skew tradeoff by sampling the design space and adapting selection strategy based on feedback.

title: Automated Generation of Decoders for Irregular Instruction Sets Using Information-Theoretic Decision Tree Construction Algorithms
problem: Manual design of instruction decoders for complex ISAs is tedious and error-prone; existing automated decoder generation tools cannot handle irregular instruction sets with non-uniform opcodes, complex logic propositions, and nested specializations.
method: Proposes sophisticated decision-tree algorithm based on information-theoretic concepts for automated decoder generation. Algorithm optimizes tree structure considering both functional correctness and performance costs using decision tree generation principles from machine learning.

title: Single Spike Artificial Neural Networks
problem: Standard ANNs require large-scale arithmetic with high energy consumption, while spiking neural networks (SNNs) circumvent this via biologically inspired computation but use fundamentally different algorithms from ANNs, preventing reuse of the mature ANN software stack and optimization techniques. The paper seeks an intermediate approach that achieves the energy efficiency of SNNs while remaining compatible with ANN algorithms and toolchains.
method: The design represents each ANN weight as a delay element and each activation magnitude as the arrival time of a digital signal. Complete ANNs are built on top of these temporal primitives through: (1) spatial and temporal reuse strategies enabling classical dataflows (e.g., weight-stationary) in a systolic array; (2) a noise-tolerant temporal summation operation for accumulation; (3) novel hybrid digital/temporal memory circuits for storing inter-layer activations; and (4) a temporal memory integration that manages activations between layers while preserving ANN algorithmic compatibility.

title: Hydra: Harnessing Expert Popularity for Efficient Mixture-of-Expert Inference on Chiplet System
problem: Mixture-of-Expert (MoE) models suffer from extensive all-to-all communication between tokens and expert replicas across chiplets, as well as redundant computations in softmax gating for underutilized experts. These bottlenecks degrade performance and energy efficiency on distributed chiplet architectures.
method: Hydra employs a popularity-aware expert mapping strategy in software: routing tokens to experts based on expected gating distribution to minimize all-to-all communication volume. In hardware, it uses Content Addressable Memory (CAM) to eliminate explicit token permutation operations (replacing expensive SpMM unscrambling) and introduces a redundant-calculation-skipping softmax engine that bypasses unnecessary exponential/division for low-probability experts.

title: VISTA: Optimizing GPU Scheduling through Versatile Locality-Aware Data Sharing
problem: GPU thread scheduling typically overlooks data locality patterns across non-adjacent warps and CTAs, missing opportunities to reduce memory traffic through intelligent scheduling that exploits non-adjacent data sharing.
method: VISTA is a smart locality-aware GPU scheduler that dynamically identifies data locality patterns at CTA and warp levels at runtime, making intelligent scheduling decisions to improve data reuse and reduce unnecessary memory accesses for memory-intensive applications.

title: Ragnar: Exploring Volatile-Channel Vulnerabilities on RDMA NIC
problem: RDMA NICs in data centers face underexplored hardware contention-based side-channel vulnerabilities that enable covert communication and sensitive data extraction.
method: RAGNAR uses comprehensive microbenchmark reverse engineering to analyze RDMA NICs at multiple granularity levels, constructs hardware-contention-based volatile-channel attacks, and demonstrates covert channels and side-channel attacks on distributed databases.

title: Efficient Continuous Logic Optimization with Diffusion Model
problem: Logic synthesis optimization flows require exhaustive search over exponentially large transformation sequences to improve quality of results (QoR). Existing Bayesian optimization and reinforcement learning methods struggle with efficiency due to the discrete, combinatorial nature of the problem.
method: The approach optimizes synthesis sequences in a continuous latent space by leveraging a diffusion model to map between continuous points and feasible transformation sequences. Gradient information is extracted from a learned QoR surrogate model (trained to predict area/delay), enabling efficient gradient-based optimization while the diffusion model ensures solutions correspond to valid synthesis transformations.

title: CRUSH: A Credit-Based Approach for Functional Unit Sharing in Dynamically Scheduled HLS
problem: Dynamically scheduled high-level synthesis (HLS) generates dataflow circuits where each compute unit is replicated per operation, wasting area when multiple operations could share a single functional unit. Existing resource sharing approaches for dynamic HLS are unsafe because handshake-based flow control can cause deadlock when units are shared without proper backpressure management.
method: CRUSH introduces a credit-based token mechanism for functional unit sharing in dynamic HLS dataflow circuits. Each shared functional unit is associated with a credit counter that tracks available slots; producers consume a credit before issuing an operation to the shared unit and regain it upon completion. This credit-based backpressure propagates through the handshake network to ensure the shared unit is never over-committed, preventing deadlock. CRUSH is integrated as a compiler transformation pass on top of the existing dynamic HLS flow.

title: BatchZK: A Fully Pipelined GPU-Accelerated System for Batch Generation of Zero-Knowledge Proofs
problem: GPU-accelerated zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) systems optimize for low single-proof latency but do not support high-throughput batch proof generation, creating a bottleneck for applications like blockchain and verifiable ML that require generating many proofs concurrently.
method: BatchZK constructs a fully pipelined GPU execution engine for batch ZKP generation. The pipeline overlaps the multiple stages of proof generation (e.g., polynomial commitment, multi-scalar multiplication, NTT) across multiple concurrent proofs using GPU streams and memory management strategies that keep GPU compute units busy throughout. By co-scheduling proofs at different stages simultaneously on the GPU, BatchZK amortizes memory transfer and kernel launch overhead across the batch, maximizing GPU throughput. The system targets standard ZKP schemes (e.g., Groth16 or PLONK-family) that underpin modern blockchain applications.

title: FATE: Boosting the Performance of Hyper-Dimensional Computing Intelligence with Flexible Numerical DAta TypE
problem: Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) requires high-precision representations for cosine similarity calculations, making multiplication-heavy computation expensive on resource-constrained edge FPGAs. Binary HDC reduces cost but degrades accuracy significantly.
method: FATE introduces a per-dimension mixed numerical data type scheme for HDC, applying different quantization bitwidths to different dimensions of the hypervector based on their importance. This is combined with sparsity to further reduce computation. The co-design targets embedded FPGA deployment and leverages the observation that not all HDC dimensions contribute equally, enabling high-accuracy inference at lower average precision than uniform quantization.

title: Sphinx: A High-Performance Hybrid Index for Disaggregated Memory With Succinct Filter Cache
problem: Range indexes for disaggregated memory architectures suffer from excessive network round trips during tree traversal and inefficient node-based caching, limiting lookup performance for variable-length keys.
method: Sphinx replaces sequential tree traversal with parallel hash reads using an Inner Node Hash Table, reducing network round trips. A Succinct Filter Cache further minimizes network overhead while maintaining a small, coherent computing-side cache.

title: ResISC: Residue Number System-Based Integrated Sensing and Computing for Efficient Edge AI
problem: Edge AI on power-constrained devices requires efficient sensing and processing; conventional image processing and CNN inference consume significant power; integrated sensing-computing can reduce data movement but requires novel processing paradigms.
method: ResISC uses residue number system (RNS) for efficient computation: in-sensor residue encoder converts images directly to RNS in analog domain, RNS-based CNN accelerator processes RNS data using SOT-MRAM cells, and mixed-radix unit performs efficient RNS activation operations. Selective channel deactivation reduces overhead.
